name: Christopher’s At Wrigley Mansion
line: The Heater That Made The Patio
lede: A new restaurant at Phoenix’s historic Wrigley Mansion needed a patio to meet demand, and the patio needed heat that suited a 1931 landmark. Freestanding Eclipse heaters now arch over the tables, warmth and light in one.

hero.caption: Bromic-published photograph from the case study.

photos.caption: The terrace below the mansion at dusk. Bromic-published photograph from the case study.
Bromic-published photograph from the case study.

beats: Completed in 1931, the Wrigley Mansion is a Phoenix landmark with a view over the city skyline. Owner Jamie Hormel and restaurateur Christopher Gross, partners of more than 15 years, opened a new Christopher’s there, with a new patio.
To meet demand the restaurant needed the patio, and the patio needed heat. Architect Wendell Burnette had to find heaters that fit the historic design and the atmosphere of the space.
Working with Bromic’s heating experts, Burnette chose the Eclipse Smart-Heat Freestanding: an electric heater with dimmable LED lighting built in, standing beside each table and reaching over it.

quote.text: We had to find the right heater or we couldn’t do the patio, that’s what it came down to.
